context.objective: Document how we carry out Facility Compliance & Borrowing Base Certification, the controls and what needs confirmation.

turns.text: As facility preparer I start from the executed facility agreement and current amendments when certification is due. We refresh the investor commitments, tiers and outstanding balance, calculate borrowing capacity and prepare the lender's certificate. Independent review and Director review precede authorized signature. The owner's name and exact facility formulas still need confirmation.
What determines when the certification is due?

The lender specifies the certification schedule in the current executed facility agreement or LSA and amendments. Due dates differ by facility. We track lender and LPA deadlines separately. Riverwood's example says biweekly for tracker updates, but the actual interval and meaning still need confirmation; it is not a company-wide certification frequency.
After the authorized signature, what happens to the certificate, and how is it sent to the lender?

Once signed it goes through the lender-approved channel by the facility-specific deadline. We save the delivery record and lender acknowledgment or questions and answer from approved sources. Submission owner, cutoff and form of acceptance vary by facility; I don't know the exact values here. After acceptance the preparer updates the tracker and puts the legal records, calculation, review, signed certificate, submission and correspondence in digital-binder category L.
What does the independent reviewer check in the borrowing-capacity calculation?

The reviewer independently re-performs key formulas and checks borrower/investor inputs, tier eligibility and exclusions, advance rates, concentration caps, effective step-downs and the agreement-defined controlling limit, including any aggregate or LPA cap. They compare outstanding principal to lender support and compare terms, amendments, dates and deadlines. The Director reviews before signature. I have no authoritative facility-specific rate or example of an actual facility formula.
What can happen if a certification is late or the borrowing-base calculation is wrong?

A wrong calculation can misstate capacity and leave a draw or breach undetected. A late certificate can mean a missed facility deadline. We look to the executed documents or lender notice for the required corrective action, log the deadline and responsible people, track completion and lender confirmation, and escalate anything late or unclear. A capital call goes through FA-01 and FA-19A only when it is the approved remedy. Specific legal consequences are for client or counsel.
What does the Director review before the certificate is signed?

The package presented for Director review contains the certificate figures tied to the calculation and supporting records, current legal statements and attachments, comparison to the last certification, and independent review of the terms, formulas and deadlines with comments resolved. Director-level review is required before authorized signature. The source does not give the Director's separate checklist or the prescribed sign-off record.
What part of preparing or reviewing these certifications tends to take the most effort?
